title: Keeping records for a service business
audience: Owners and office staff of small service businesses in Australia who keep job, payment, tax and staff records, and who need a routine that makes the books and the evidence of each job easy to check.
referencesAtStart: Official sources used: ATO, Record keeping tips (last updated 25 October 2022); ATO, Key superannuation rates and thresholds: super guarantee (last updated 17 April 2026, page metadata).
learningOutcomes: Keep a job record for each booking that links the quote, the condition record, the invoice and the payment.
Reconcile the bank account and the GST ledger each month, and resolve any difference before the next month begins.
Write a retention schedule that states how long each kind of record is kept and when it is disposed of.

instruction.heading: What must be kept, and for how long
instruction.body: The ATO's employment and payroll records guidance says employee payment and PAYG withholding records are kept for 5 years, but the Fair Work Ombudsman says time and wages records are kept for 7 years, so the schedule must not apply the 5-year period to time and wages records. The period runs from the later of when the record was made or obtained, and when the transaction or related act was completed. Where a review period runs longer, the records must be kept until that period ends. For a service business, the records to keep include records of all cash and electronic transactions, including reconciled card and EFTPOS sales; records that support business expenses claimed as deductions; records of the business portion of an expense that also has private use, such as a vehicle or a phone; a separate GST ledger account where GST credits are claimed; and PAYG payment summaries for amounts withheld from payments. This is a teaching summary, not the full list, so check the ATO page for the complete list before you set the schedule. Superannuation paid for staff is recorded against the payroll, and the general super guarantee rate for the period is 12.00 per cent from 1 July 2025.

instruction.heading: The job record as the evidence for each job
instruction.body: A job record is the single file that proves what was booked, what was agreed, what was done and what was paid. Open it when the booking is confirmed, not after the job. Attach the quote, the booking confirmation with the included and excluded items, the pre-work condition record and the photographs, and the consent for photographs where it was given. Add the time on site, the products and consumables used, the handover note and any complaint. Then link the invoice and the payment, so that the income, the deposit and the balance can each be traced to the job. Store photographs under the job number, not in a general camera roll, so that they can be found when a client raises a question months later. Keep the record secure, and limit who can open it. When a client asks for a copy, check what the record contains before sending it, and remove any information that does not belong to that client. The job record is also the source for the complaint register, so a complaint should always point back to the job it concerns.

instruction.heading: The monthly routine: reconcile, check GST, prepare the BAS
instruction.body: A monthly routine keeps small problems small. Each week, file receipts and supplier invoices against the job or the expense type they belong to. Each month, reconcile the bank account: match every bank line to a receipt, an invoice, a payment or a transfer, and note any line that cannot be matched. Check that the GST ledger balances against the sales and purchases recorded for the period, and that client deposits are still held as liabilities for jobs not yet completed. Record PAYG withholding and superannuation for staff as they are incurred, not when the bill arrives. Good practice is to base each business activity statement on complete and accurate records rather than estimates. Ask your registered tax agent for the lodgement and payment schedule that applies to your business. Keep the reconciliation sheet with the month's records, so that anyone checking the books can see how each difference was resolved.

procedure: Set up the record types in one place: job records, bank records, GST ledger, payroll and PAYG records, contractor records and the retention schedule.
Open a job record for each booking when it is confirmed, and attach the quote and the booking confirmation.
Attach the condition record, the photographs under the job number, and the consent for photographs.
Link the invoice and the payment to the job, and record deposits as liabilities until the job is completed.
Each week, file receipts and supplier invoices against the job or the expense type they belong to.
Each month, reconcile the bank account and the GST ledger, and resolve every unmatched line before closing the month.
Record PAYG withholding and superannuation for staff in the period they are incurred.
Write the retention schedule with the 5-year general period, the review-period caveat, the disposal date and the person who approves disposal.

workedExamples.situation: In an example, at month end the bank statement shows a $150 deposit from a client. The same $150 has been recorded as income, but the job is not yet done because the client has booked a service for next week. The job record for that booking is open and has the quote and the booking confirmation attached. The $150 figure is invented for this example and is not a price.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you correct the books, and what do you record in the job record?
workedExamples.reasoning: The income entry is wrong, because the job has not been completed. Reverse the income entry and post the $150 to the client deposits liability account, linked to the open job record. Note the correction and the date in the reconciliation sheet, so that the change can be seen. When the service is completed, move the deposit from the liability account into service income and link the invoice.

equipmentAndPpe: Accounting software or spreadsheet with the chart of accounts from “Chart of accounts for a service business”.
Secure cloud folder or locked filing for job records, with access limited to named people.
Scanner or phone scanning app for receipts and signed handover notes.
Calendar with the reconciliation, BAS and disposal dates marked.
No personal protective equipment is needed for this desk-based routine.

commonErrors.error: Keeping job photographs on a phone with no link to the job or the client.
commonErrors.prevention: Store each photograph under the job number at the time it is taken, and back it up to the secure folder.

commonErrors.error: Recording a deposit as income before the job is completed.
commonErrors.prevention: Post deposits to the client deposits liability account, and move them when the job is complete.

commonErrors.error: Mixing personal and business card payments in one account.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a separate business account and post owner withdrawals to drawings.

commonErrors.error: Preparing a business activity statement from memory or from estimates.
commonErrors.prevention: Draw the figures from the reconciled bank records and the GST ledger for the period.

commonErrors.error: Deleting records before the retention period has ended.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the retention schedule with the records, and do not dispose of a record until its period and any review period have ended.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The ATO's general retention guidance is 5 years, with a longer period where a review period runs beyond that, as stated on the ATO record-keeping tips page last updated 25 October 2022. Recheck the page before you set a disposal date.
Client records include personal information and photographs of a client's property. Keep client records secure, use them only for the job, and limit who can open them.
Whether contractor payments must be reported, and the lodgement schedule for the business activity statement, depend on the business. Confirm both with a registered tax agent.

qualityStandard: Every job has a record that links the quote, the condition record, the invoice and the payment.
The bank account and the GST ledger are reconciled every month, and every unmatched line is resolved or recorded as open.
Deposits held for jobs not yet completed sit in a liability account at month end.
The retention schedule is written, dated and approved, and no record is disposed of before its period has ended.
documentationEvidence: Job record with quote, booking confirmation, condition record, photographs with consent, invoice, payment and handover note.
Monthly reconciliation sheet showing the bank, the GST ledger, the corrections made and the open items.
Retention schedule with record types, retention period, disposal date and the approver.
summary: Open a job record when the booking is confirmed, and link it to the invoice and the payment.
Reconcile the bank and the GST ledger every month, and keep the reconciliation with the records.
Keep records generally for 5 years, time and wages records for 7 years, longer where a review period runs beyond that, and write the schedule down.

knowledgeChecks.question: According to the ATO guidance, how long are most business records generally kept?
options: Until the business closes, with no set period for any record at all, whatever the type, the year, the amount or the client involved in the job
Only until the next business activity statement is lodged with the ATO for the quarter, the year and the whole period of the records held in the file
Generally 5 years from the later of when the record was made or the transaction was completed, and longer where a review period runs beyond that

knowledgeChecks.question: Why match the job record, the invoice and the payment for each booking?
options: It is only needed for staff wages and the tax on them, the super and the payroll
It lets you check that income, deposits and payments line up and that nothing is missed
A tax agent can skip it when the amounts are small and round and easy to check

knowledgeChecks.question: The bank shows a deposit that has also been recorded as income, but the job is not done. What is the fix?
options: Leave both entries and wait for the business activity statement to arrive from the ATO next quarter
Delete the bank line so the figures agree for the year end, the books, the summary and the report
Correct the entry so the deposit sits as a liability until the job is done, and note the change
